items.problem: `start_boot` records the boot entry scene only when the module list is omitted, so a boot entry scene that passes a module list is never destroyed. `open-game-works-core/skills/client-core/modules/bootstrap-core.md:32` allows the boot entry scene to pass a list, and `bootstrap-core.md:67` says a successful `TitleScene` destroys that scene. Reproduced in a temporary copy of the target commit with a throwaway test: a new node set as `tree.current_scene`, then a boot with `_SUPPORT.modules()` up to `BootCompletedEvent` plus 3 frames, and the node is still valid. This is not caused by the commit range.

no core test goes through the destruction of the boot entry scene. Every `start_boot` of the core tests passes a non-empty list (`tests/support/boot_test_support.gd:266`, `tests/test_boot_order.gd:247`, `tests/test_boot_dev_run.gd:188`), so `_boot_entry_scene` stays `null`. In a temporary copy of the target commit, replacing `_boot_entry_scene.queue_free()` with `pass` still gives `ogw core test godot BootstrapCore` pass on the native run. This is not caused by the commit range.

`open-game-works-core/skills/client-core/modules/bootstrap-core.md:266` requires that `content_release` is not called on a restart or app exit during `Update` and on a `shutdown` before `ContentInit`, and no test covers these three cases. The tests assert `release_count` 0 only for an update reboot (`tests/test_boot_restart.gd:156`), a restart in `TitleScene` (`tests/test_boot_restart.gd:171`) and an exit in `TitleScene` (`tests/test_boot_exit.gd:85`). No test halts in `BootStage.UPDATE`, and no test that calls `shutdown` before `ContentInit` asserts `content_release`. By reading, the implementation guard `_content_inited` (`client/godot/core/bootstrap_core/bootstrap_core.gd`, `_reverse_release` and `_shutdown`) gives the required result, so this is a missing test and not a wrong result. This is not caused by the commit range.
